citations.note: Broadly consistent with (not contradicting) the existing 29 °C Canadian field-pea flowering/pod-abortion figure. Does not add a stage timing or Moroccan validation. The ECOCROP tutorial (.research-sources/2026-11-06/ecocrop-tutorial.pdf, p.2) defines TOPMN/TOPMX as 'the optimal growing temperature adaptability range (the range of temperatures under which the plant will grow optimally)' and TMIN/TMAX as part of 'the full growing temperature adaptability range (the full range of temperatures under which the plant will grow)... All entries are absolute values.' Neither definition states a daily-maximum or daily-minimum air-temperature basis, a duration, or a growth stage; ECOCROP's underlying climate matching (Hijmans et al.) compares these to long-run mean monthly temperatures, not single-day extremes. TMIN/TMAX are therefore NOT used here as whole-cycle damage limits outright; they are recorded as the closest FAO-tier evidence with this basis gap explicit in missingFields. The builder could not re-find the quote in the saved text, so it is not reproduced.

references.summary: Cool-season annual; the catalog crop is vegetable green pea. Seedlings and flowers differ in frost sensitivity; cold-hardy field-pea results need product and cultivar context. Hot weather around flowering and pod set can reduce fertility and accelerate loss of tenderness. Cereal breaks can interrupt some pea disease cycles; other legumes may share pathogens or pests. Green-pea harvest precedes dry-seed maturity; dry field-pea cycle lengths should not be substituted.
